title: Machine learning-guided synthesis of two-dimensional AgBi iodide perovskites
summary: The authors combined an 80-amine high-throughput synthesis dataset, chemistry-informed molecular descriptors, subgroup discovery and a support-vector classifier to rank organic spacers for 2D AgBi iodide perovskites. Of 13 model-selected candidates taken forward, eight were successfully synthesized and characterized by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and powder X-ray diffraction. The study reports a 61.5% success rate in this selected validation set; it does not establish universal synthesis performance across other perovskite families.
ai_technology: Subgroup discovery and support-vector classification using physicochemical and molecular-topology descriptors

evidence.tested: The primary article reports successful synthesis of 8 of 13 machine-learning-selected 2D AgBi iodide perovskites (61.5%), with crystal structures determined by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and bulk-phase purity confirmed by PXRD.
evidence.unknown: The validation concerns a selected set under common laboratory synthesis conditions and one AgBi iodide family; generalization to other material families is not demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Subgroup discovery identifies an applicable data region and a support-vector classifier estimates synthesis feasibility from molecular descriptors; the model ranks candidate organic spacers for experimental synthesis.

source_review.scope: Primary Nature Communications publisher PDF indexed full text including Results, Methods, author contributions and article metadata; Southeast University institutional announcement checked for corroboration.
